newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico criticized, expelled human rights workers. [CORRECTED 04:25 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Mexico criticized, expelled human rights workers. [CORRECTED 04:25 GMT]

text.p: An international human rights group blasted the Mexican government on Monday for expelling two Central Americans investigating violence in the troubled Mexican state of Guerrero.

The two Central Americans, one from Nicaragua and the other from El Salvador (corrects), left Mexico abruptly on Sunday, the deadline set by Mexican immigration authorities, who discontinued their tourist visas.

"The decision taken comes in the context of growing repression against defenders of Mexican human rights," Patrick Baudouin, president of the International Federation of Human Rights Leagues (FIDH), said in an open letter to Mexican President Ernesto Zedillo.
The federation is headquarted in Paris.

Two federation human rights workers, Vilma Nunez of Nicaragua and Benjamin Cuellar of El Salvador, had been investigating reported abuses in Guerrero, the state with the highest number of human rights complaints in Mexico, the organisation said.
Baudouin said in the letter to Zedillo that their expulsion was "a flagrant attack on the freedom of action for human rights defenders" that are protected in international conventions.
